extraction.Name: David Mesteth
extraction.Refused/Protested: did not want his patent in fee when it was issued, September 29, 1929, covering his 160 acre allotment; but he was informed that, if he did not take it, and pay the taxes on his land, taxes would accumulate on it anyway, and his land finally be sold for same; so he took the patent in fee
extraction.Sold/Mortgaged: sold it in the spring of 1920, to De Mullen Loan Company, of Hot Springs, South Dakota, for $800.00 cash
extraction.Buyer: De Mullen Loan Company, of Hot Springs, South Dakota, for $800.00 cash
extraction.Tax burden forced sale/Mortgage: he could not pay taxes on his land, that he sold the allotment; also sold his place for debts incurred prior to receiving his patent in fee, as he was considerably in debt when he received it
extraction.Occupation/Income: farms his wife's land, and sells hay and wood, for his living; and that these are the sources of his income
extraction.NOTES: Allotment of 160 acres; mentally competent, has good health; has a wife and five children to support; family has fair health; considers he received but a fair price for his land; never received any help from the County, State nor the United States Government; document sworn April 3, 1929 (fee patent date of September 29, 1929 may be an error in the document, as the affidavit is dated April 3, 1929)
